- If sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) in recent days, reduce forecasted peak values to avoid over-optimism.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a forecasted decline, adjust downward by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are flat or declining, reduce forecasted highs to avoid lagged momentum misalignment.  
- If forecasted price exceeds true outcome by >10% in early days of the 30d window, apply a downward correction proportional to sentiment magnitude.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is volatile or mixed, cap the forecast at the 30-day moving average of recent history to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days preceding forecast, apply a 3–5% downward bias to all forecasted values.
